And now we have nothing left in all the land of Sinjar
except this fortress of Tikrit.
And this man,
that is to say, the Caliph,
has wished to strip even this from our hands.
Therefore we beg that you come without delay and drive him away from it."
Then the people of Mosul gathered immediately,
and went forth, directing their course towards Tikrit.
Then the Caliph, when he heard that they were prepared and coming against him,
fear fell upon him,
and he abandoned all the baggage and the weapons of war,
and went to Baghdad.
And after some days, a certain Turkish emir gathered about twelve thousand [men],
and sent and brought Arslan Shah, son of Toghril the Seljuk, out from the prison of Tikrit,
for the sake of the name, saying that someone of the royal line of the Seljuks was with them;
and he set out.
The Caliph also went out with his forces to meet them.
And after eighteen days during which they remained encamped opposite each other beside the road to Khorasan,
they clashed with one another.
And the Caliph's flank was broken,
and he wished to flee.
Then two of his officers persuaded him to hold out a little,
and by force they urged his horse forward.
And the Baghdadis took courage,
and turned back against the Turks,
and shattered them and put them to flight,
and took all their baggage.
And it is said
that they plundered four hundred thousand sheep from the Turks,
apart from oxen and camels.
And in this year, the waters of the Tigris ran like blood, exceedingly red;
and also in various places in the region of Wasit, blood welled up from the earth,
and no one knew the cause of this.
And in the year 1467
(1467 of the Greeks,
and 1155? of our Lord), the Prince, the lord of Antioch, went to war with Thoros, the ruler of Cilicia,
because the Franks were claiming those fortresses which the Armenians had taken from the Greeks,
so that they might belong to the Fratres {Knights Templar/Hospitaller},
whose toil is on behalf of all Christians,
to possess them,
because the Greeks had taken them from the Franks.
And the Armenians resisted.
And the two sides clashed with one another at the gate of Sunkraton (or of Sequntaron);
and the Armenians were defeated,
and Thoros fled.
And then he made peace,
and gave those places to the Fratres.
